course_description:
Design, implementation and presentation of a research project, with emphasis on defining the research issue, establishing methodology, undertaking appropriate analysis of data and drawing defensible conclusions. Students completing the course in one semester must enrol in AGRC7617. Students completing the course in two semesters must enrol in AGRC7620 if they plan to commence in semester 1 and AGRC7621 if they plan to commence in semester 2. Students must submit the Research Project Contract by the first Thursday of February for students commencing in semester 1, and the first Thursday of July for students commencing in semester 2.

NOTE: Students completing their project at St Lucia or at an external institute should enrol in the Gatton Internal mode of offer. Contact agriculture@enquire.uq.edu.au for enrolment queries. Students enrolled into a 2 year Masters program should not enrol into this course until they have completed 16-units of study (2 semesters full-time equivalent) Students enrolled into a 1.5 year Masters program should not enrol into this course until they have completed 8-units of study (1 semesters full-time equivalent).

The student will select a topic for their research in discussion with a university supervisor. The topic may be investigated through a range of approaches including - but not limited to - fieldwork, laboratory work, computer analysis and use of surveys.

Enrolment in this course

This course has an enrolment permission list in Si-net and only students with an approved Application Learning Contract are allowed to enrol. Students must work with their academic supervisor to complete the Application Learning Contract and submit it by the first Thursday of February for students commencing in semester 1, and the first Thursday of July for students commencing in semester 2.

If the Application Learning Contract is approved, the student will be given permission to enrol in the course.

At the School of Agriculture and Food Sustainability, we are committed to creating an inclusive and empowering learning environment for all students. We value and respect the diverse range of experiences our students bring to their education, and we believe that this diversity is crucial for fostering a rich culture of knowledge-sharing and meaningful exploration. We hold students and staff accountable for actively contributing to establishing a respectful and supportive learning environment.

Bullying, harassment, and discrimination in any form are strictly against our principles and againstﾠ UQ Policy, ﾠand will not be tolerated. If you have any concerns about your experience in this course, we encourage you to tell a member of the course teaching team. Your well-being and a positive learning atmosphere are of utmost importance to us.

Additional timetable information
Students are expected to interact regularly with their University supervisor, and to actively engage with other students and researchers working within the selected work group or lab.
Students must schedule meetings (preferably weekly) with their supervisor and ask for feedback as they progress.
An orientation lecture and induction session are timetabled for Week 1 of Semester. Students are expected to attend.
Check-in/advisory sessions are scheduled for Week 4 and 7. Please attend if you have any questions about research or your specific project.
Students are required to attend the scheduled seminar sessions in Week 13, this is where In Person students will present live in class, alongside students from the other AGRC-research project courses.
If you have any questions about missing class activities, please contact your course coordinator.
course_aims: To introduce students to the activities involved in carrying out a research project.

learning_outcomes.description: Define a problem, state a hypothesis and propose a process for the investigation of the problem.
Design and implement a research project, analyse and interpret data, discuss results and draw relevant conclusions.
Produce a research report in the form of a potential journal article.
Deliver an oral presentation on a defined topic.
Demonstrate professional behaviour in the context of the researchable topic, in consultation with the supervisory team

assessment_details.title: Sequential mid-project assessment
assessment_details.task_description: Component 1 - Research Proposal (20%) A written assessment whose aim is to provide students with the tools to more effectively manage their project as well as allow the opportunity for a personal reflection. This will be marked by your principal supervisor. The purpose of this 4-part mid-project assessment is to a) articulate your research problem early on b) encourage conceptual organisation c) promote professional reflection on complex issues around supervision, communication and project management d) foster the use of ubiquitous project management tools such as mind maps and GANTT charts and e) enable responsible use of generative AI. N.B. You will not be penalised if your research strategy changes after this assessment piece is submitted. Indeed, adaptation, pivots and change are acknowledged as a normal and healthy part of research science. This is intended to be a constructive process – not a punitive one. The assessment will a) introduce you to tools and processes that help scientists meet deadlines without undue stress and time pressure but also b) support productive change, should the evidence indicate to you and your team that change is required. You are given 4 tasks to complete: · Proposal / strategy document (1 page) · Mind map (1 page) · GANTT chart (1 page) You are encouraged to develop these in consultation with your project supervisor WITHOUT recourse to AI. Once you have mature drafts of all three in place you are then encouraged to use a generative AI system of your choice for provision of feedback and suggestions for improvement. The assessment document available on BB includes some links to supporting Freeware. Acknowledging and/or referencing AI use Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Machine Translation (MT) are emerging tools that may support students in completing this assessment task. Students may appropriately use AI and/or MT in completing this assessment task. Students must clearly reference and acknowledge any use of AI or MT in each instance. A failure to reference and acknowledge generative AI or MT use may constitute student misconduct under the Student Code of Conduct. The use of AI or MT must be referenced and acknowledged appropriately. The use of AI and / or MT must be acknowledged using a statement recorded on the coversheet. The statement must contain a description of the AI system that has been engaged and detail around the nature of use. Please see assessment guidelines in blackboard course site for specific instructions. Students may also refer to Library guides found under Additional assessment information > Acknowledging and referencing AI use. Component 2 - Reflection (Complete/Incomplete hurdle) You will complete a professional reflection and questionnaire (there are 13 questions to guide your reflection). This will be reviewed by the course coordinator. As part of your professional reflection, you will then be asked to make specific comments on the utility of generative AI in the context of these 3 activities. You are encouraged to develop your personal reflection in consultation with your supervisor. You MUST NOT use generative AI to help you write your personal reflection. The assessment document available on BB includes further information. Read full task description Hide full task description

assessment_details.submission_guidelines:
Submit an electronic copy either as a word or pdf file via Turnitin to the relevant submission link in the course Blackboard site by the submission deadline. You should also retain an electronic copy of every piece of assessment you submit.
Legal Declaration:
By submitting your work via this website, you formally declare that (1) it is your own original work, and no part of the work has been copied from any other source or person except where due acknowledgement is made; (2) no part of the work has been previously submitted for assessment in this or any other institution; and (3) you have read the Student Integrity and Misconduct Policy and understand its implications.
Deferral or extension
You may be able to apply for an extension .
The maximum extension allowed is 28 days. Extensions are given in multiples of 24 hours.
Submission of an Extension of Assessment Due Date (EADD) should be completed online through your My Requests tab via my.UQ Dashboard , in accordance with the University's Assessment Procedure (located in the Policies and Procedures section of this course profile) which outlines the requirements for requesting extensions to assessment due dates.
Extensions require the correct evidence/documentation to support the requested length of time of the extension. This may also require a statement from your supervisor(s) outlining the reason for extension, impacts to the student, the project and supported length of extension.
Late submission
A penalty of 10% of the maximum possible mark will be deducted per 24 hours from time submission is due for up to 7 days. After 7 days, you will receive a mark of 0.
For example, a report worth a maximum of 40 marks, submitted 28 hours late will incur a penalty of 8 marks. This is calculated as 2 (24 hour periods) x 10% per period x 40 marks, resulting in 8 marks deducted from the student’s mark for the assessment.
Assessment deadlines are firm and must be met. Late submission without permission or non-submission of assessable work will result in penalties being applied . Late submission of assessment will only be granted for documented medical reasons, accident, bereavement, jury service and other circumstances allowed in the UQ Policies and Procedures Library (PPL).

assessment_details.title: Research Project Report
assessment_details.task_description: The research project report is to be presented in the form of a scientific manuscript potentially suitable for publication in a professional journal. The exact length and structure of your report may vary across disciplines – please seek specific advice from your supervisor regarding your interpretation of these guidelines. Broadly speaking, we anticipate the report consisting of a title, abstract (< 300 words), introduction / background / literature review (< 600 words for science reports, but a much longer, more comprehensive literature review for social science and agribusiness reports), methodology including statistical analysis (< 2000 words), results (< 2000 words), discussion (< 1500 words), conclusions (< 200 words) and references. In general concision is encouraged, the upper word count limits are to be considered guidelines only and represent a conversation starter for discussion with your supervisor. Two independent examiners who specialise in your area of research will mark your work. The average of your marks from both markers will be used as your grade. In the event that there is a difference of more than 10 points between markers your report will be sent to an independent marker and a decision made which may involve taking the average of the 3 marks. This assessment item is not eligible for a re-mark as it has been independently marked by two examiners and has undergone the prescribed moderation and review processes. As a result, there is no further academic judgement to be reconsidered through a re-mark process. Students who believe an administrative error has occurred (for example, an error in mark calculation, data entry, or grade recording) may submit a query to the course coordinator for review. Any identified administrative errors will be corrected where appropriate. Students may appropriately use AI and/or MT in completing this assessment task. Students must clearly reference and acknowledge any use of AI or MT in each instance. A failure to reference and acknowledge generative AI or MT use may constitute student misconduct under the Student Code of Conduct. The use of AI or MT must be referenced and acknowledged appropriately. The use of AI and / or MT must be acknowledged using a statement recorded on the coversheet. The statement must contain a description of the AI system that has been engaged and detail around the nature of use. Please see assessment guidelines in blackboard course site for specific instructions. Students may also refer to Library guides found under Additional assessment information > Acknowledging and referencing AI use. Marking timeframes are expected to be at minimum two weeks, for independent markers to review your work fairly and comprehensively. assessment_details.title: Performance as determined by project supervisor
assessment_details.task_description: Your academic supervisor will assess your overall performance through the life cycle of your research project. 'Performance' here includes the indicators below that your supervisor deems of relevance to your circumstances: 1) Evidence of planning & time management. 2) Evidence of punctuality. 3) Evidence of resourcefulness. 4) Evidence of independence. 5) Evidence of creativity. 6) Evidence of 'managing up' well. 7) Evidence of determination, and other positive temperamental characteristics, in overcoming challenges. 8) Evidence of strong inter-personal communication. 9) Evidence of integrity and ethical awareness. 10) Evidence for record keeping Students are not required to submit this assessment item. AGFS Admin will contact your principal supervisor directly with the marking rubric, and will work with them to have the assessment item completed and returned. policies_and_procedures: University policies and procedures apply to all aspects of student life. As a UQ student, you must comply with University-wide and program-specific requirements, including the: Student Code of Conduct Policy Student Integrity and Misconduct Policy and Procedure Assessment Procedure Examinations Procedure Reasonable Adjustments for Students Policy and Procedure AI for Assessment Guide Recording of Teaching Policy and Procedure Learn more about UQ policies on my.UQ and the Policy and Procedure Library . You'll also need to be aware of the following policies and procedures while completing this course: Occupational Health and Safety in the Laboratory Guideline Vaccinations and Immunisation Procedure Course guidelines Student immunisation requirements - as per individual student project requirements. The University policy Vaccination and Immunisation ( Vaccinations and Immunisation Guideline / Document / Policy and Procedure Library ) provides information about immunisation and screening requirements related to programs and courses. Failure to comply with student immunisation requirements can lead to an increased risk of serious illness occurring. Therefore, non-compliance will result in the relevant course/s being dropped from your enrolment under Section 3 of the Enrolment policy ( Enrolment Procedure / Document / Policy and Procedure Library) .
